punchline: A plane crash makes headlines because it is frightening, while the thousands of safe landings go unreported.
thirty_sec: Hans Rosling says frightening and dangerous are different things. Fear sends our attention to unlikely dangers like physical harm, captivity or contamination, and away from what is most risky. A plane crash makes the news, while the safe landings never do. His fix is an equation: risk equals danger times exposure. So calm down first, then calculate. He explains it in Factfulness.
